- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast by 1–2% for consecutive high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices after recent spikes (forecast peaks > true peak by 3%+) — adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast rises sharply after a dip, reduce by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal triggers: if sentiment drops below 0.4 after peak, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate by 1–3% in early cycles — apply 1% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or declining.
